The Confederation of African Football has increased its financial support to member associations from $200,000 to $700,000, its President, Patrice Motsepe, has said. Motsepe disclosed this on Saturday during a press conference after the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of CAF in Abuja. He said the increase was part of efforts to strengthen the financial capacity of the 54 member associations and promote the development of football across the continent. According to him, the governing body had initially set a target of providing $1m to each member association but was currently paying $700,000. “Our million-dollar objective is paying very well. We’ve paid $700,000 without the money that was going to come from our commission,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. We are now paying $700,000 from $200,000,” he added. The CAF president also disclosed that the organisation had committed substantial resources to competitions, prize money and other football development programmes. Motsepe said the organisation’s financial support programmes were aimed at making African football more sustainable and reducing the dependence of member associations on external funding. He added that increasing resources available to national football associations remained a priority for his administration. “We need to increase the resources, financial resources, and the money that our member associations get, and the money from FIFA,” he said. The CAF president said his administration was working towards leaving African football in a stronger financial position before the end of his tenure.
